deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): ε is a primitive cube root of unity. Gauss sets (α+βε+γε²)³ = A+Bε+Cε², with
A = α³+β³+γ³+6αβγ,
B = 3(α²β+β²γ+γ²α),
C = 3(αβ²+βγ²+γα²).
He has already noted the identity (B−A)³+(C−A)³+(2A−B−C)·N = 0, where N = (A+Bε+Cε²)(A+Bε²+Cε) = A²+B²+C²−AB−BC−CA.
[My step: this is just x³+y³=(x+y)(x²−xy+y²) with x=B−A, y=C−A, since x²−xy+y² = N.]
N is the norm of a cube, so N = Q³ with Q = α²+β²+γ²−αβ−βγ−γα. The scheme therefore produces solutions of X³+Y³ = k·Z³ with k = B+C−2A. The page studies which k arise. The previous page lists numerical cases such as 19³+18³ = 37·7³ and 19³+1 = 20·7³.

This page:
(1) The standard factorization: (α³+β³+γ³−3αβγ)/(α+β+γ) = Q.

(2) In elementary symmetric functions s1 = α+β+γ, s2 = αβ+βγ+γα, s3 = αβγ, the coefficient is 2A−B−C = 27s3 + s1(2Σα² − 5s2) = 2s1³ − 9s1s2 + 27s3.
[My verification: Σα³ = s1³−3s1s2+3s3 and Σ_sym α²β = s1s2−3s3.]

(3) Specialize to s1 = 0. Then:
- A = 9αβγ.
- B−A = 3P, with P = α²β+β²γ+γ²α−3αβγ = αβ(α−γ)+βγ(β−α)+γα(γ−β).
- C−A = 3R, with R = αβ²+βγ²+γα²−3αβγ = αβ(β−γ)+βγ(γ−α)+γα(α−β).
- 2A−B−C = 27αβγ.
Dividing by 27 gives P³+R³+αβγ·Q³ = 0, which Gauss writes out. [The factor-27 bookkeeping is mine.]

(4) He also records Σα³ = 3αβγ + (3/2)s1·Σα² − (1/2)s1³ (Newton/Girard).

(5) He eliminates γ = −α−β in P, computing the terms α²β+β²γ, γ²α and −3αβγ separately. Summing gives P = α³+6α²β+3αβ²−β³.
[My completion: similarly R = −α³+3α²β+6αβ²+β³, αβγ = −αβ(α+β), and Q = 3(α²+αβ+β²).]
The resulting two-parameter identity is
(α³+6α²β+3αβ²−β³)³ + (−α³+3α²β+6αβ²+β³)³ = 27αβ(α+β)(α²+αβ+β²)³.
This expresses 27αβ(α+β)·(cube) as a sum of two cubes. The purpose is to find integers k for which X³+Y³ = kZ³ is solvable, via cubing elements of Z[ε].
errors: No mathematical errors found; all identities check.

In the last computation the term +γγα appears struck out in the first line, yet Gauss's expansion includes it (the line α³+2ααβ+αββ is γ²α with γ=−α−β). The result α³+6α²β+3αβ²−β³ is the correct value of P including that term, so the deletion is not reflected in the computation (or was a deletion of the '=' sign, not of the term).
Gauss leaves Q unsimplified in the s1=0 case; Q = −3s2 there. This is not an error, only incomplete simplification.

symmetric-function expansion (resembles the discriminant-related cubic invariant 2s1³−9s1s2+27s3)

results.what: For α+β+γ=0: P³+R³+αβγQ³=0 with P,R cyclic cubic expressions
results.modern_name: norm-form construction of solutions of X³+Y³=kZ³ via cubes in Eisenstein integers
results.usually_credited_to: Euler / Lagrange-style method; systematic treatment Sylvester, Lucas, Pépin, Desboves (19th c.)

results.modern_name: classical parametric identity for sums of two cubes equal to k·cube (related to 3-isogeny/Hessian of x³+y³=kz³)
results.usually_credited_to: appears in 19th-century literature (Desboves/Lucas type formulas; cf. Dickson History vol. II); also in Ramanujan-style identities

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's interest in X³+Y³=AZ³ and in arithmetic of Z[ε] (cubic residues, Fermat n=3) is well documented in his Nachlass. The parametric identity is classical-looking and was known in the 19th century. The page is careful exploratory algebra rather than a new theorem.
